$comment: The application descriptions this site's copy was written from. Updated only by `npm run copy:accept`, which is the explicit act of saying the words here have been re-read against the words there. Never edited by hand and never refreshed to make a test pass.

all-accounts-one-page.name: Every account in one place
all-accounts-one-page.plain: See what you have across every bank account, card, and wallet on a single page, in whatever currency each one is in.
all-accounts-one-page.why: Most people's money is spread across five or six logins and nobody adds it up.

import-statements.name: Bank statements that file themselves
import-statements.plain: Upload the file your bank gives you. It works out the layout, sorts the payees and categories, and flags anything that looks like a duplicate before it counts.
import-statements.why: Typing in transactions by hand is the reason most people quit after two weeks.

numbers-that-tie-out.name: Numbers you can actually check
numbers-that-tie-out.plain: Every figure can be traced back to the entries behind it. When something looks wrong, you can open it up and find the row that caused it.
numbers-that-tie-out.why: The common complaint about budgeting apps is that the totals do not agree and there is no way to find out why.

own-your-data.name: Your data stays yours
own-your-data.plain: Run it on your own machine and nobody else has a copy. Export every transaction to a spreadsheet whenever you want.
own-your-data.why: It is a record of everything somebody spends money on.

budgets.name: Budgets that roll over
budgets.plain: Set a limit per category. What you do not spend can carry into next month, and money you get refunded goes back into the budget it came out of.
budgets.why: A budget that resets to zero every month is one people abandon in March.

recurring.name: Nothing to remember
recurring.plain: Rent, payday, a subscription: set it up once and it shows up when it is due, waiting for you to approve it.
recurring.why: The annual renewal nobody remembers is the classic way a budget gets blown.

find-anything.name: Find any transaction
find-anything.plain: Search and filter everything you have ever entered, by payee, category, account, amount or date.
find-anything.why: "When did I last pay for that?" is the most common question anybody asks their own records.

duplicates.name: No duplicates
duplicates.plain: Import the same statement twice and it shows you the rows you already have instead of adding them again.
duplicates.why: Importing twice is easy to do and tedious to undo.

multi-currency.name: More than one currency
multi-currency.plain: Hold accounts in different currencies. Totals are kept separate rather than converted at a rate that would be out of date tomorrow.
multi-currency.why: Anybody who has moved to another country, works abroad, or travels has this problem and most tools guess at it.

categories.name: Spending by category
categories.plain: Group your spending the way you think about it, and see where the money actually went.
categories.why: It is the first question people ask and the last one most tools answer clearly.

splits.name: One receipt, several categories
splits.plain: Split a grocery run between groceries and household, each counted on its own.
splits.why: A supermarket trip is rarely one category.

bulk-edits.name: Fix thousands of rows at once
bulk-edits.plain: Change or delete up to ten thousand transactions at once, after seeing exactly what it will touch.
bulk-edits.why: One mis-mapped import can put a year of entries in the wrong category.

templates.name: Templates for repeat entries
templates.plain: Save the transactions you type over and over and reuse them in a click.
templates.why: Cash spending is the part nobody imports, and typing it is the part nobody keeps up.

register.name: A running balance for every account
register.plain: Every entry with the balance before and after it, so you can find the exact point a figure went wrong.
register.why: This is how you reconcile against a real bank statement.

history.name: Nothing is ever quietly overwritten
history.plain: Corrections are added on top rather than replacing what was there, so the history of a mistake survives the fix.
history.why: It is the difference between a record and a guess.

agents.name: Let an AI assistant do the filing
agents.plain: Connect an assistant and let it import statements and clean up categories. When you connect it you see exactly what it is asking to do and can refuse; an assistant limited to suggesting queues entries for you to approve, and Settings shows what each connected assistant can do and lets you cut it off.
agents.why: It is genuinely useful and genuinely alarming, so the limits matter more than the capability.

payees.name: Everywhere you spend
payees.plain: A list of everyone you have paid, and everything you have paid them.
payees.why: It is how you notice the subscription you forgot about.
